rationale: Each horizontal pair becomes one cell: [2,2] gives 2, [3,0] gives 0, and [0,0] gives 0. Preserve only uniform nonzero pairs.
Each 3x3 block becomes 5 when it contains any nonzero cell; entirely zero blocks become 0. The third demonstration's sparse bottom-middle block still gives 5.
Take the most common colour in each horizontal pair, including background: [3,3] gives 3, while [0,1], [2,0], and [1,0] give 0 on ties.
Take the most common colour in each vertical pair, including background: two 2s give 2, two 3s give 3, and mixed zero/nonzero pairs give 0 on ties.
Each 2x2 block preserves its colour only when all four cells share a nonzero colour. Solid 2 and 3 blocks survive; diagonal coloured cells among zeros give 0.
Each uniform nonzero 3x3 block becomes its colour. In the second demonstration, solid 1 and 3 blocks survive while blocks containing both zeros and colour become 0.
Reduce each 2x3 block to its colour only if all six cells are the same nonzero colour. The first solid 2 block gives 2; partially filled 1, 2, and 3 blocks give 0.
Each 2x3 block containing any nonzero cell becomes 5. In the third demonstration, a block with just one 1 gives 5, while entirely zero blocks give 0.
Choose the most common non-background colour in each 2x3 block, or 0 if empty. A lone 1 among five zeros gives 1, and two 3s among four zeros give 3.
Each vertical pair preserves a shared nonzero colour: [1,1] gives 1 and [3,3] gives 3. Mixed pairs such as [1,0] and [0,3] give 0.
